title: Folded threads annotary and runtime probe sketch
content:
TL;DR
Quick synthesis of recent field threads about runtime surprises (latency spikes, soft-fallbacks, KV cache regressions) + a compact set of low-touch probe experiments we can run in the next 2–4 sprints. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: pick two probes, run them against 10 customers, measure delta on latency P95 and token-cost per session.

Sources & sampling
- Collected from: support transcripts (Feb–Mar 2026), two SRE runbooks, three customer calls (large fin-tech, mid-market search SaaS, ML platform team), and a quick survey sent to 14 heavy-hosted API customers.
- Sampling note: heavy bias toward revenue-tier customers who run long-chat sessions and high-embedding volumes. Not exhaustive for PLG tail.

Key themes (high-level)
1) Silent regression: customers reported intermittent 150–300ms P95 jumps on generations after a week-long period where no config changed. Triage points at autoscaler interactions and KV cache eviction heuristics.
2) Fallback opacity: when the platform silently routes to a cheaper model during congestion, customers see output deviation but no clear signal in logs or console explaining the fallback decision. They want observable reasoning messages and a way to opt-out per-route.
3) Billing friction with embeddings: customers are unsure why some embeddings calls consume more tokens; misunderstandings around conversation context trimming and system-prompt concatenation. They want clearer token previews and cheaper short-embedding paths.
4) Streaming + function-calls flakiness: some SDKs drop the final tool call event intermittently under sustained streaming load. Affects webhook-based pipelines.

Representative quotes (unedited snippets)
- "We saw a step-change in cost last Wednesday, and we can't tell if it's the model change or our users talking more." — FinTech infra lead
- "Fallbacks are great but when they change answers we spend hours chasing it. Need an audit trail and a 'do not fallback' flag." — Search team PM
- "Embeddings cost exploded. We accidentally sent system messages per-item in a batch. We need a preview before we blast 10k rows." — ML platform eng

Top feature asks (prioritized)
1) Fallback transparency UI + per-route opt-out (Impact: H, Effort: M):
   - Acceptable first pass: console flag + timeline showing fallback events (time, target model, reason code). Add a simple queryable API for events.
   - Why: reduces customer toil, increases trust.
   - Data to show: deviation metric on representative prompts pre/post fallback.

2) Token preview & batch sanitizer for embeddings (Impact: M, Effort: S):
   - Lightweight client-side utility in SDK: compute tokens per-row and highlight rows that will cause token blowup. Also provide an option to compress context automatically (truncate system messages for embeddings).

3) KV-cache eviction telemetry + autoscaler correlation (Impact: H, Effort: L–M):
   - Emit a compact KV-cache event stream for customers (optional): cache hits/misses per route plus reason codes for eviction (memory pressure, TTL, model shift). Correlate with autoscaler actions.

4) Streaming reliability patch & checklist (Impact: M, Effort: M):
   - Short-term: patch SDKs to rehydrate final function-call event on reconnect. Long-term: add end-to-end fuzz/replay tests for streaming+function calls.

Quick probes (pick 2)
A) Synthetic replay with golden prompts (SLO vs. fallback events) — owner: eng-sre (Marco)
   - Run: replay 10k sessions with customer-provided golden prompts across two quotas: normal and constrained (force fallback). Measure: P50/P95 latency, answer-drift score (BLEU-ish/cosine over embeddings of outputs), token-cost delta.
   - Success signal: measurable drift > 5% when fallback triggered and clear mapping from fallback events to drift.

B) KV cache pressure smoke test (owner: serving-runtime)
   - Run: synthesize many unique long-conversation sessions to force KV churn; compare eviction reasons with autoscaler logs. Measure customer-observed latency jumps and cache-miss rates.

C) Embedding batch preview beta in SDK (owner: devx)
   - Lightweight release to 5 customers: SDK emits token-preview warnings and optional compactify flag. Measure reduction in token-cost mistakes and number of support tickets referencing "embedding surge."

Engineering notes & blockers (observed from triage)
- There's low-fidelity event tagging around fallback decisions. We currently log model_id but not the decision policy metadata (cost vs latency vs region).
- KV-cache internals: eviction reasons are encoded but not surfaced beyond infra logs — need a thin proxy to surface to per-customer console.
- Autoscaler timescales: when autoscaler spins up nodes, there is a 20–40s window where routing may favor variants; customers feel this as a spike.
- SDKs differ in reconnect semantics for streaming; reproducer exists for Node and Python.

Risks & open questions
- Surfacing fallback reasons could leak internal pricing logic — legal review needed for messaging templates.
- Token preview heuristics might be imperfect for customers that use private prompt-engineering conventions (we must allow opt-out).
- Synthetic replays may not capture real user diversity; pair with small live A/B on dedicated customers.

Proposed immediate next steps (this week)
- Pick probes A + C (SRE + DevX) and spin up 2-week spike: scope concrete measurement plan, pick 5 participating customers, draft consent note. Owner: Aisha (CS) + Marco (SRE).
- Draft a fallback transparency spec (customer-friendly language) for legal review. Owner: Leah (CS) + Omar (Product).
- Create lightweight JIRA tickets: CS-5127 (probe coord), ENG-2345 (kv telemetry proxy), DEVX-78 (embedding-preview SDK).

Notes to self
- Keep probes surgical: we want signal, not a full rewrite.
- For customer outreach, prepare a one-paragraph ask: what we will run, what we will measure, what we need from them (sample prompts, opt-in).

Appendix: measurement templates we will use
- Latency: P50/P95/P99 before/during/after probe window (30min buckets).
- Drift: cosine similarity between embeddings of outputs for golden prompts; human-check if similarity < 0.85.
- Cost: token-cost per session and per-turn.

End of sketch.

Unresolved: do we want to include a "do-not-fallback" per-route header now or ship the UI first? Recommend API flag + console visibility in parallel.
